name: Burundi
snapshot: One of the world's poorest countries, dominated by the ruling CNDD-FDD, which won every elected seat in 2025, and drawn into the Congo war next door.
culture: Burundi's royal drummers, who perform on huge drums carried on their heads, are on UNESCO's heritage list and were once tied to the monarchy's rituals. Kirundi is spoken by almost everyone, giving the country a rare linguistic unity. Hills, banana groves and family compounds define rural life, and Lake Tanganyika's shore is the country's main leisure space.
society: Most Burundians are subsistence farmers on tiny plots, in one of Africa's most densely populated countries. Coffee and tea are the main exports, and fuel and foreign currency shortages are chronic. The 1993 to 2005 civil war between Hutu rebels and the Tutsi-dominated army killed some 300,000; the peace deal built ethnic quotas into government and the army.
baseline: President Évariste Ndayishimiye succeeded Pierre Nkurunziza in 2020. The ruling CNDD-FDD won all seats in the 2025 legislative election after the main opposition figure, Agathon Rwasa, was sidelined. Burundian troops are deployed in eastern Congo against the Rwanda-backed M23, deepening hostility with Rwanda, and the fall of Bukavu in 2025 sent refugees across the border.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Nestor Ntahontuye, since August 2025
